full_judgment: 16. A presumption of lawfulness exists, in the first instance, in favour of every consideration and the law presumes against illegality to start with. To bring a case within the purview of section 23 of the Contract Act, it is necessary to show that the consideration or object of an agreement is forbidden by law or that it would defeat the provisions of any law or is fraudulent or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another or is immoral or opposed to public policy. If the object or consideration is unlawful, the agreement becomes void. There is absolutely nothing to show that the present contract is forbidden by law or comes within the mischief of any other provision of section 23 of the Contract Act.
